newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares fall to close, seen weaker.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares fall to close, seen weaker.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares continued largely weaker on Wednesday, with brokers pointing to new issues on the exchange which they said had drained a lot of money off the market.

"The market was a little bit busier today -- we saw some volume coming back but generally it's still weak. A lot of money still hasn't come back to the market from the new issues and things should continue that way for quite a while," one broker commented.
The key industrial index shed 57.16 points to close at 10,426.22, largely weighed down by a 50 cent loss to 1,700 in blue chip conglomerate Delta, in heavy turnover.

Other major losers included sugar firm ZSR which dropped 100 cents to 1,400, while clothing retailer Truworths put off 50 cents to 1,000. Paper firm Hunyani at 320 and financial group Finhold at 730 were both 20 cents weaker.

Minings were more active but prices remained largely unchanged. The seven-counter index added 8.47 points to 965.54, mainly on the back of a 50 cent gain in gold miner Rio Tinto, which gained 50 cents to 2,350, with Falgold putting on five cents to 75 cents.
